title: Review of c42's slow-fuel ecology: replicates on fresh seed 5 (128^2, t=12000): segregated predator worm patch and prey droplet field, predators alive at the end (8 components), prey 8 persistent splits (generation 2) vs 4 (generation 1) in the predator-free twin; predators 0 persistent splits, merge/split 1.7
summary: Ran c42's world.py with WORLD_P {"Du":0.3} and its predator-free twin ({"Du":0.3,"pred_on":0}) on unused seed 5 (labkit, 128^2, 120 frames = t=12000). Real: predators form a worm-like network in a waste-rich patch while prey droplets fill the rest, the boundary shifting slowly (du3/seed5/sheet.png); predator components 8 at the end (max 34), 0 persistent splits, merge/split 1.69; prey 38 droplets at the end, 89 splits, 8 persistent, generation 2. Twin: frozen emulsion of 103 prey droplets, 4 persistent splits, generation 1. Same direction as c42's 14/8/3 vs 0/5/1, with a smaller gap on this seed.

observations.X: du3/seed5/sheet.png: standing segregated predator and prey zones to t=12000; prey persistent splits 8 vs 4 in the predator-free twin

seeds_run.result: pass (predators persist; prey divide more than in the twin)

verdicts.limitation: One seed; the prey division excess over the twin is 8 vs 4 here, small. Predators do not reproduce (0 persistent splits), so the ecology is not yet reproducing on both sides.
